decision: Deferred. Sharing one worktree scan among a save's readers measured no faster than today's four readers, and no repository in use is past 8,655 tracked files.
scope: The worktree reads a save starts: get_status, get_dirty_counts, the graph refresh's dirtiness read, get_wip_diff_stats. Backend probe only; the page trial was run at 20,000 and 30 files.
comparativeVerdict: Hypothesis refuted: status beside the WIP diff alone (the shared-scan end state) is no faster than all four readers.
machine: Apple M5 Pro, 48 GB, macOS, shared with other sessions

procedure: t489 <repo> mixes: for each round, each set of readers starts on its own threads at one instant, and the status thread's finish time is recorded. Readers: status (dirty_status_options plus renames_head_to_index), counts (same options), graph dirtiness (dirty_status_options), WIP diff (tree-to-index plus index-to-workdir with untracked content).

repositorySizes.command: for d in ~/code/*/; do git -C "$d" ls-files | wc -l; done

profile: sample of 15 status scans at 100,000 files: lstat in about 420 of 720 samples, in libgit2's single-threaded scan
limitations: The non-monotone cost in the number of concurrent scans was not explained.
The page trial was not run at 100,000 files.
Untracked trees of this size were not generated.
The machine was shared with other sessions' work.
